narratives.Overview:
## Problem

A subagent that does no work and reports success is recorded as a successful completion. Nothing on the dispatch path compares a worker's completion claim against the artifact it claims to have produced, so a fabricated handback is indistinguishable from a real one.

Measured on this host, 2026-08-30, during two design-critique panels. Two dispatches of the same critic seat returned completion claims naming GitHub comment ids that do not exist. Both were recorded by the harness as `success: true`, `error: null`.

| Attempt | Duration | Inference loops | Tool calls | Claimed artifact | Reality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 9.4 s | 2 | 4 | comment 5470174383 with finding counts | 404; no comment on the thread |
| 2 (re-dispatch with an explicit read-back postcondition) | 1.8 s | 1 | **0** | comment 5470572756 with finding counts | 404; no comment on the thread |

Sibling seats on the same envelope, same panel, same round, for comparison: 11-43 inference loops and 38-57 tool calls each, all producing real posted artifacts.

The second attempt made zero tool calls in 1.8 seconds. It could not have read the contract it was told to read, let alone measured anything or posted. It still returned a well-formed DONE line with plausible per-class finding counts, and the harness booked it as a success.

## Why existing surfaces miss it

| Surface | What it stops | Why it did not stop this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evaluateParentTurnShape` (#3131 / FC14) | Repeated parent assistant text with no tools | This is a *child* turn, and the parent was issuing tools normally |
| Delivery-attempt ledger (#3143) | Re-dispatch of a dead unit, budget exhaustion | The dispatch completed and reported success; no budget was exceeded |
| Dual stop (#2442) | Iteration without progress | One turn, reported complete on the first pass |
| `verify:subagent-alive` (#2824) | A worker that stopped heartbeating | The worker did not stop; it exited claiming success |
| Design-critique dispatch-failure halt | A spawn that dies or posts nothing | Only fires if the parent independently checks for the post |

The only thing that caught it was the parent choosing to read the claimed comment id back over REST. That is operator diligence, not a control.

## Consequence in the design-critique motion

The contract forbids binding a synthesis while a same-round sibling is unposted. A parent that trusts the handback would have counted three posts, bound a two-of-three panel, and produced a completed-arc record that clears ingest -- with one seat's findings invented. The panel-completeness obligation is already documented as behavioural with no predicate observing it (#3850), and this is the failure mode that makes that gap reachable without an adversary.

The same shape generalizes past design-critique: any orchestrator that fans out work and aggregates DONE messages inherits it.

## Ask

Make a worker's completion claim checkable at the dispatch boundary, or make the absence of work detectable.

Two candidate shapes, both deterministic:

1. **Artifact postcondition in the dispatch envelope.** The envelope declares what must exist when the worker exits (a comment id on an issue, a file at a path, a pushed branch). The orchestrator verifies existence before accepting DONE. Failure is a dispatch failure, not a success.
2. **Zero-work detection from host telemetry.** A completion with zero tool calls, or with a tool-call count below a declared floor for the task class, is surfaced as a suspect completion rather than a success. The host already records `tool_calls` and `turns` on the completion event, so the signal exists without new instrumentation.

Shape 2 is cheap and catches the blatant case. Shape 1 is the real control and catches a worker that does *some* work and still lies about the outcome, which is what attempt 1 above did.

## Acceptance

- A dispatch envelope can declare a verifiable postcondition, and a completion that fails it is classified as a dispatch failure rather than a success.
- The classification is deterministic and does not depend on the orchestrator remembering to check.
- A unit test reconstructs both attempts above: zero-tool completion with a claimed artifact, and partial-work completion with a claimed artifact that does not exist. Both fail closed.
- The design-critique panel path consumes it, so a same-round sibling that did not post cannot be counted toward panel completeness.
- Do not close by adding prose telling orchestrators to verify handbacks. That is the current state and it is what failed.

## Non-goals

- Deciding which model or provider is at fault. The routing decision for the specific model involved is recorded separately as a decision record; this issue is about the harness accepting an unverified claim regardless of which model produces it.
- Detecting deception in general. The scope is a checkable postcondition, not intent.

## Evidence pointers

- Host log records for the two dispatches (`subagent completed`, `success: true`, `error: null`, `tool_calls` 4 and 0).
- Design-critique arc on #3961: dispatch-failure record, halt line, and operator resume verb on that thread.

## Verdict on the refutation target

Re-verified at pin `704db5564313741fd07d9e3092420ad149f01e16`. The target premise (harness may accept child `success: true` / a well-formed DONE without a declared artifact postcondition, with operator REST read-back as an acceptable control) does **not** hold as a safe design claim.

Evidence from tree inventory (not from issue-body narrative):
- No dispatch-boundary artifact-postcondition verifier on child DONE / spawn completion acceptance under `packages/` at this SHA (search for postcondition/claimed-artifact/comment-existence gates returned unrelated body/migrate/init postconditions only).
- `evaluateParentTurnShape` (`packages/core/src/parent-turn-shape/`) is parent-turn FC14 only.
- `evaluatePreDispatch` / delivery ledger (`packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/`) gates retry/re-dispatch of failed or budget-exhausted units; a completed success claim does not enter that breaker.
- Dual-stop design-critique (`content/contracts/design-critique.md` Dual stop): dispatch-fail is spawn-died / no comment posted, and only when the parent surfaces that evidence; parallel panel completeness stays behavioural (#3850). `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` treats a panel-deposit as in-flight and does not count critic posts against `siblings:`.
- `verify:subagent-alive` (`packages/cli/src/verify-subagent-alive.ts`) is heartbeat/STALE liveness; a worker that exits claiming success is outside REDISPATCH_OK.
- Launch-probe / `evaluateN3LaunchProbe` dispatch-fail covers pre-spawn posture, not post-completion artifact truth.

So P1–P3 remain live at the pin. Operator diligence is the only catch named in-ceiling, which the AC forbids as a close.

## Findings

### F1 — Acceptance choke point under-specified relative to AC and #3850
**class:** `blocks-the-design`

**evidence:** Stop 1 Prefer-A names an envelope-declared postcondition “checked before accepting DONE,” and AC requires classification that “does not depend on the orchestrator remembering to check,” plus design-critique panel path consumption. Contract text at this SHA still states panel completeness is behavioural with no predicate observing sibling posts (#3850 / `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` deposit-as-in-flight only). No host/Directive acceptance adapter that rewrites child `success: true` → dispatch-failure on missing artifact was found.

**failure mode:** A Bound remedy that ships a callable verifier library (or skill prose) while the host/parent path still books `success: true` on the handback recreates the measured hole: a fabricated comment id is counted, synthesis can bind on a partial panel, ingest-ready clears.

**disposition consequence:** Cannot bind Prefer-A unless Bound remedy names the choke point that reclassifies completion **before** success is accepted for that dispatch (host completion adapter and/or a mandatory consumption path on the design-critique panel that cannot treat an unverified handback as a posted sibling). Optional parent diligence remains out of AC.

### F2 — Shape 2 alone cannot carry AC
**class:** `sharpens-framing`

**evidence:** Stop 1 Prefer-A already ranks shape 1 as the real control and shape 2 as complementary. AC requires unit fixtures for both measured attempt classes: zero-tool claimed artifact, and partial-work claimed artifact that does not exist. Shape 2 (tool-call floor / zero-work telemetry) covers only the blatant zero-tool class.

**failure mode:** A lean that binds telemetry-floor-only as the acceptance control passes the cheap case and still books attempt-1-class lies as success.

**disposition consequence:** Bound remedy may keep shape 2 as a cheap complementary signal; it must not substitute for shape 1 when claiming AC satisfied.

### F3 — Adjacent #3120 handoff-evidence must be placed, not ignored
**class:** `sharpens-framing`

**evidence:** At this SHA, `packages/core/src/handoff-evidence/validate.ts` already fail-closes `invented-done` / `empty-done` for structured handoff evidence with remote PR/SHA/CI/review claims requiring same-turn probes. That surface is builder/pre-pr/review-cycle handoff shape, not host spawn-completion acceptance, and not a GitHub issue-comment id postcondition for design-critique critics.

**failure mode:** Implementing Prefer-A without naming extend-vs-new either duplicates probe grammar in a second module or leaves #3120 unused while reinventing bound-proof, splitting “invented remote claim” doctrine across layers.

**disposition consequence:** Bound remedy must record whether comment-id (and file/branch) postconditions extend the #3120 probe/bind model or are a distinct host-boundary mechanism, and keep the two consumers explicit.

### F4 — Untrusted child artifact ids need definite-vs-indeterminate verify classes
**class:** `sharpens-framing`

**injection / swarm lens:** Target changes dispatch authority, treats child DONE text and claimed ids as untrusted input, and sits on concurrent panel fan-out over shared issue-thread state.

**evidence:** Prefer-A’s existence check is the control; child-supplied comment ids / paths / branch names are claims. Contract already refuses counting self-attested `role: critic` lines as panel-complete.

**failure mode:** Trusting the child’s id string, or collapsing transport/auth errors into “missing,” either success-washes a lie or thrash-halts healthy seats on flake.

**disposition consequence:** Bound remedy names independent verification (REST GET / fs / git), and separate fail-closed classes for definite absence vs indeterminate probe failure, mapped to dispatch-failure without requiring a new Dual-stop halt token.

### F5 — First-ship surface vs whole-harness blast
**class:** `sharpens-framing`

**evidence:** Issue Ask generalizes to “any orchestrator that fans out”; AC requires the design-critique panel path to consume the control. Stop 1 spend reason is high-blast harness fan-out plus open shape choice.

**failure mode:** An unbound “universal host gate for every fan-out” Prefer-A stalls implement or ships an unbounded surface; a design-critique-only count gate that never reclassifies host success fails the Ask’s dispatch-boundary clause (see road-not-taken).

**disposition consequence:** Bound remedy records first-ship surface (at minimum: declared comment postcondition + success reclassification on the design-critique panel path) and what is deferred for general fan-out.

### F6 — Prose outcome rules do not close this
**class:** `footnote`

**evidence:** `content/coding/coding.md` Fail Loud (#1006) obligates outcome-verified completion claims in agent prose; it is not a harness gate on `success: true`. AC already forbids a prose-only close.

**disposition consequence:** Census only; no residual.

## Road not taken

**#3850-only sibling-count gate** inside `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` (compare live `role: critic` posts in-arc to panel-deposit `siblings:`) without host success reclassification.

**Steelman:** Smallest Directive-side change; directly blocks the stated consequence (bind/ingest on a missing seat); stays off host telemetry; aligns with existing completed-arc fixtures.

**What would flip toward that alone:** If AC dropped “dispatch envelope / completion classified as dispatch failure” and the Ask narrowed to design-critique bind-only. At the recorded AC and Ask, that road is insufficient: attempt-class fixtures and harness acceptance still pass.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `evaluateParentTurnShape` | yes | no (parent FC14) |
| Dual-stop / leftover-pain | yes | no (success claim ≠ dispatch-fail unless parent detects missing post) |
| Delivery-attempt ledger | yes | no (success path) |
| `verify:subagent-alive` | yes | no (liveness, not artifact truth) |
| Design-critique dispatch-fail / launch-probe | yes | no (spawn/probe; post-completion artifact unchecked; #3850 unobserved) |
